notes: Summary: Mid-market product analytics platform evaluating Redwood Hosted API first, POC then shifting to Dedicated. Primary goal: fast in-app assistant + semantic search with predictable unit economics and data isolation.

Initial outreach: inbound from product team via blog post; demo 2025-11-12 (recorded, see Fireflies). AE Sofia did high-level demo: streaming chat + embeddings routes. SE Liam joined to discuss latency targets and infra.

POC scope (started 2026-01-22): 4-week proof to validate 95th pct latency <200ms for short chat turns (256 tokens), embedding throughput 200 qps, and prefix cache effectiveness for common flows. POC used hosted API with request routing to small dedicated pool.

POC results (2026-02-05): latency met for chat (p95 ~165ms avg), embeddings throughput consistent at ~220 qps. Observed 18% token cost reduction with prefix caching and batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.

Security review: submitted security questionnaire 2025-12-01; procurement requested SOC2 Type II evidence and company policy on KMS & key segregation. Legal asked for data residency commitment for EU customers (they have EU customers). SE provided Redwood SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes (drive link).

Decision drivers: predictability of cost (finance prefers committed price), ability to burst for growth events (product launches), VPC deployment for customer data, and contractual SLAs for latency and uptime.
Pricing discussions (multiple calls: 2026-02-10, 2026-02-18):

- AE proposal A: 12-month Dedicated commitment = baseline capacity (equiv. 2x A100) with monthly commit credit and burst pool up to +2x for 24 hours/day with burst throttling. Base commit pricing ~$10k/month, estimated ARR $120k.
- AE proposal B: 6-month ramped commit: month1 50% baseline, month2 75%, month3+ full. Lower up-front commit discount, slightly higher overall unit price. CFO prefers this for cashflow protection.

- Overage / burst pricing: suggested overage at $0.018 per 1k tokens above commit; burst allowance charged at 150% of base rate if sustained >24h. Mentioned capacity-based overage ($/GPU-hour) as alternative if they prefer predictable compute lines.
- Ramp protection ask: customer requested a cap on effective overage charges for first 3 months post-commit (suggested cap = 20% of monthly commit). AE to escalate to pricing committee.

SE notes on technical tradeoffs: recommended dedicated KV cache warm-up policy and reserve prefix cache slots to minimize burst cost. Also suggested split routing: high-SLA chat on dedicated, lower priority reranking on hosted (cost-savings).

Legal / procurement items: standard SOW + Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with EU residency clause. Procurement asked for sample SOW with explicit ramp schedule and termination terms tied to commit months.

Commercial status: internal pricing committee reviewed on 2026-02-25. Pricing options being finalized. AE proposed final offer to include: 9-month committed term, 3-month ramp schedule, burst pool 1.5x for 48 hours, overage cap 25% for first 90 days, 10% prepayment discount.

Customer feedback: Product lead (Raj) said: 'we like predictability — can we get a clear per-token committed rate and a simple overage cap? We need to avoid surprise bills during launches.' CFO asked for monthly cost simulations under 3 growth scenarios (base/expected/high).
Open questions we need to resolve before close:
- Finalized committed baseline (GPU count vs tokens/day) — AE to propose two concrete tiers by 2026-03-03.
- Confirm EU data residency language in DPA — legal to provide redline by 2026-03-08.
- Overage mechanics: $/1k tokens vs $/GPU-hour — CX preferred tokens pricing but finance wants compute clarity.
Timeline / next steps:
- 2026-03-01: pricing committee draft sent to customer (email thread).
- 2026-03-03: AE to present two concrete commit tiers and pro-forma invoices (done by Sofia).
- 2026-03-08: Legal DPA redline due from Redwood legal.
- 2026-03-15: target SOW signature and kickoff of on-premises/VPC onboarding calendar.
